## Backlog — High priority (the top of the queue)
| B-2026-09-23-6 | **Duplicate files of any kind, judged by content not filename — the next session's focus, raised by the user.** A registry of file families, each climbing the same cheap→expensive ladder: identify, describe, hash the *payload* (not the file, so retagging does not hide a duplicate), and only where that cannot settle it, the expensive perceptual probe. Songs are the motivating case, not the scope. The brief carries the boundary-test constraint, a per-family feasibility table, the verified stdlib tier, the decision about where a package this size may live, and four questions to put to the user first: `.context_ledger/memory/office/plans/duplicate-files-brief.md` (working spike beside it). |
| B-2026-09-23-7 | **Show the page the browser world is driving, and what the run actually saw of it.** The engine already has `cdp.screenshot()`, `BrowserEnvironment(screenshot_dir=...)` and a `screenshot` action; the CLI uses them via `--shots`. The gap is one call site — `worlds.py::_browser_world` never passes `screenshot_dir` — plus a panel, a frame-per-decision written beside the run (not inside the artifact), and a `window.tm` channel to read one. **The agent reads text, never pixels**, so the panel must show the page *and* what the run extracted from it, distinguishably; a bare screenshot would imply the agent saw what the viewer sees. Sharpens B-2026-09-23-2 for the browser. Brief: `.context_ledger/memory/office/plans/browser-what-it-sees-brief.md`. |
| B-2026-09-23-8 | **Draw the branches, not just the path — the alternatives are folded and nothing renders them.** The engine probes *and scores* every candidate at each step and applies one; across the saved runs that is 186 decision points and 54 alternatives discarded. `foldDecisions` already folds them into `Decision.options: Candidate[]` with the world's answer and the evaluator's score on each — and `grep '\.options' panels/ shell/` returns nothing. Add sibling stubs at each tree node (leaves, never subtrees — they were probed once), the alternatives in the ledger row, and the count in the tree header. **Necessary but not sufficient:** the maze branches 1.35 ways per decision, so this pairs with B-2026-09-23-9 (a world that actually branches). Brief: `.context_ledger/memory/office/plans/the-roads-not-taken-brief.md`. |
| B-2026-09-23-9 | **A world that actually branches — chess.** Measured: the maze offers **1.35 candidates per decision across 202 decisions**, so the tree reads as a line because it is one, and B-8 alone would draw 0.35 stubs per node. Chess offers ~35 legal moves per position, and unlike every shipped world its evaluations are checkable against ground truth — the ledger saying it believed a move was worth 0.7 while it hangs a queen is this product's pitch made falsifiable. ~400 lines of stdlib move generation (python-chess is forbidden by ADR-2); test with published perft counts. The action carries the position so a fan of probes cannot mutate a shared board — the pattern the maze already uses. Brief: `.context_ledger/memory/office/plans/a-world-that-branches-brief.md`. |
| B-2026-09-23-10 | **The browser world corrupts facts when two navigations share a fan — demonstrated, not theorised.** The engine probes a fan with `asyncio.gather`, concurrently, from one state; `BrowserEnvironment` holds one page. Probing `goto(example.com)` and `goto(iana.org)` together, **both observations came back "loaded https://www.iana.org/..."** — so the fact written into the state says the run went to example.com and landed at iana.org. The observation is not stale, it is false, and a false fact is the one thing this product cannot survive. The maze's docstring names this exact hazard. Real fix: a navigation action carries the URL it acts on and returns that page's own reading (ADR-4 rule 1). A stopgap guard is in `BrowserReasoner` (one navigation per fan) — the guard is not the fix, because any other proposer, including a model, can still produce the fan. |
| B-2026-09-23-11 | **Let people bring their own world.** The `Environment` protocol is four members and the README promises a new world is one row — true inside this repo, false outside it: `worlds.py` is a hardcoded dict and there is no discovery mechanism at all. Add a loader over `ti_matrix.worlds` entry points plus a `~/.ti-matrix/worlds/` directory, a template world that is correct by construction, and an order-dependence check at registration — because ADR-4 rule 1 is the rule nobody guesses and the one whose failure looks like model hallucination. Options, costs and three questions for the user: `.context_ledger/memory/office/plans/worlds-users-can-bring-brief.md`. |
| B-2026-09-23-12 | **The engine cannot tell it has been somewhere before.** Every fingerprint belongs to an action, never to a state, so two routes to one junction re-probe a cell already held as fact and the tree grows two subtrees for one place. `DESIGN.md` already ruled on which sameness to detect — *what is known*, not what was answered and not how it was reached — and `tests/test_maze_adapter.py::test_the_engine_cannot_tell_it_has_been_somewhere_before` already measures the cost. Reasoned about, asserted, and in no queue until now. The trap: `Observation.fact()` bakes the action label into the fact string, so hashing `state.facts` detects identical *histories*, not identical knowledge — the obvious implementation looks right and does nothing. Design: an optional `Environment.state_key(state)`, because a place is a world's concept and the engine is host-neutral (ADR-4); on a collision union `failed` and do not re-probe. Land it **before** B-2026-09-23-11 opens the protocol to users. Brief: `.context_ledger/memory/office/plans/same-place-different-state-brief.md`. |
